title: A modular agent-based framework for wildfire evacuation: Integrating fire spread, multimodal transport, and dynamic routing
authors: Shahab Mohammad Beyki; Anne S. Patricio; Antonio Gameiro Lopes; Aldina Santiago; Luis Laim
one_line_difference: The first wildfire evacuation model we could verify that explicitly simulates INBOUND rescue traffic and emergency extraction simultaneously with outbound self-evacuation on a fire-degraded network — it occupies the simultaneity, but the reported output is simulated evacuation time validated against a drill, not a latest-safe-dispatch deadline.

title: Setting Wildfire Evacuation Trigger Points Using Fire Spread Modeling and GIS
authors: Thomas J. Cova; Philip E. Dennison; Tae H. Kim; Max A. Moritz
one_line_difference: Founds the whole field by computing a deterministic fire-arrival level set (trigger buffer) around a community for a decision-maker-supplied evacuation time; it does not model traffic, responders, ensembles, or any dispatch deadline.

title: Design of stochastic trigger boundaries for rural communities evacuating from a wildfire
authors: Nikolaos Kalogeropoulos; Harry Mitchell; Enrico Ronchi; Steve Gwynne; Guillermo Rein
one_line_difference: Produces STOCHASTIC trigger boundaries by sampling historic wind/weather/vegetation variability and introduces 'uncertainty rosettes' mapping where the boundary is most sensitive — this is probabilistic trigger design done properly, and it is the paper that makes WG-C-004 unclaimable.

title: Quantifying dire evacuations in case of wildfire using trigger boundaries and case study of the 2018 Mati wildfire in Greece
authors: Nikolaos Kalogeropoulos; Harry Mitchell; Erica Kuligowski; Enrico Ronchi; Guillermo Rein
one_line_difference: Treats BOTH wildfire spread and evacuation time as probabilistic variables and outputs an 'evacuation safety factor' in [0,1] — a scalar decision-relevant probability of mission failure — which is structurally the same kind of output WG-C-003 wants, but computed for community egress rather than a responder round trip.

title: Defining probabilistic evacuation triggers for wildfires using an ensemble of flame spread models: The Fort McMurray case study
authors: Nikolaos Kalogeropoulos; Guillermo Rein
one_line_difference: Builds trigger boundaries from a MULTI-MODEL ENSEMBLE (Farsite, Prometheus/WISE, ELMFIRE, Google EPD, EPD-ConvLSTM) and shows the boundary location depends on which spread model you believe — this kills WG-C-004 outright and puts strong pressure on WG-C-014 and WG-C-009.

title: Setting Wildfire Evacuation Triggers by Coupling Fire and Traffic Simulation Models: A Spatiotemporal GIS Approach
authors: Dapeng Li; Thomas J. Cova; Philip E. Dennison
one_line_difference: Replaces expert-judgement evacuation time with a TRAFFIC SIMULATION, derives a cumulative probability distribution over clearance times, and emits probability-indexed trigger buffers (e.g. the 95th-percentile buffer) — this is the single closest prior art to a 'probabilistic, traffic-aware trigger', and it does it for household egress, not responder dispatch.

title: Value of information for spatially distributed systems: Application to sensor placement
authors: Malings, Carl; Pozzi, Matteo
one_line_difference: Shows explicitly that optimal sensor placement DEPENDS ON THE DECISION PROBLEM, encoded in a problem-specific loss function - the exact methodological move WG-C-008 wants to claim; domain is spatially distributed infrastructure with Gaussian random fields, not a fire front under an evacuation deadline.

title: A Relaxation-Based Decomposition Approach for Solving a Supported-Evacuation Problem in Wildfires
authors: Shahryar Moradi; Antoine Saure; Jonathan Patrick
one_line_difference: Formulates supported evacuation of people who cannot self-evacuate as a two-stage stochastic facility-location + multi-vehicle PDPTW in which BOTH the assembly area and the ROUTE carry a hard time window 'after which the route is reached by the fire' — so the inbound leg IS fire-constrained; but the time windows are drawn from Uniform(400,850) minutes rather than from a fire-spread model, and the output is a routing/fleet plan, not a latest-safe-dispatch time.

title: Forecast skill is not decision skill: evidence from weather-dependent decision tasks
authors: Raeth, Kornelius; Ludwig, Nicole
one_line_difference: States and demonstrates the general negative result WildfireGuardian wants for WG-C-014: forecast-level performance does not reliably translate to decision-level performance and model rankings change between similar decision tasks; the tasks are frost/heat protection and wind dispatch with scalar cost functions, not a spatial fire forecast scored by IoU against an evacuation-mission decision.

title: Action-BED: Task-Driven Bayesian Experimental Design with Singly Intractable Objectives
authors: Rossa, Tom; Phillips, Angus; Rainforth, Tom
one_line_difference: Reformulates experimental design as minimising expected future LOSS of downstream actions rather than information gain - decision-directed sensing as a general method, 2026; entirely domain-agnostic, no hazard, no deadline, no wildfire.

title: Decision-focused Sensing and Forecasting for Adaptive and Rapid Flood Response: An Implicit Learning Approach
authors: Sun, Qian; Hults, Graham; Xu, Susu
venue: BuildSys '25: Proc. 12th ACM Int. Conf. on Systems for Energy-Efficient Buildings, Cities, and Transportation
one_line_difference: Selects in-situ sensor locations AND trains the forecast model end-to-end to minimise downstream evacuation/relocation decision regret, explicitly rejecting information-gain placement and average-error training; hazard is flood depth, the decision is evacuation/relocation cost, and there is no responder dispatch deadline or fire-arrival feasibility constraint.

title: Operational Decision Support for Evacuating Nursing Home Residents: A Hamburg Benchmark and Metaheuristic Comparison Under a 5-Minute Time Budget
authors: Nick Alexander; Milva Tannenbaum; Jörg Noennig
venue: Proceedings of the Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference (GECCO '26)
one_line_difference: Alexander et al. minimise waiting time and makespan for shuttling mobility-impaired residents under a solver time budget; no hazard progression constrains any leg and no departure deadline is computed.

title: From forecast skill to economic value: sub-hourly wildfire potential forecasting across Australian regions
authors: Ardid, Alberto; Power, Anthony; Valencia, Andres; Pearce, H. Grant; Gross, Shana; Dempsey, David; Boer, Matthias M.
one_line_difference: This is the wildfire instantiation of the cost-loss/PEV pipeline: ML fire- potential forecasts evaluated by Potential Economic Value against the Fire Behaviour Index; the decision is pre-positioning/fire-potential warning, NOT evacuation protective action, and the FBI comparator is an operational index, not a buffer/trigger policy tuned on the same scenario distribution.

title: Are Hourly PM2.5 Forecasts Sufficiently Accurate to Plan Your Day? Individual Decision Making in the Face of Increasing Wildfire Smoke
authors: Berlinghieri, Renato; Burt, David R.; Giani, Paolo; Fiore, Arlene; Broderick, Tamara
one_line_difference: Wildfire-smoke domain: evaluates six operational forecasts on two explicit DECISION tasks against a strong persistence baseline and finds no forecast beats persistence on one task while most beat it on the other; the decision is individual exposure avoidance, not evacuation timing, and the baseline is persistence rather than a tuned spatial trigger.

title: Assessing time, cost and quality trade-offs in forecast-based action for floods
authors: Bischiniotis, Konstantinos; van den Hurk, Bart; Coughlan de Perez, Erin; Veldkamp, Ted; Nobre, Gabriela Guimaraes; Aerts, Jeroen
venue: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction
one_line_difference: Makes the timeliness-vs-accuracy trade-off explicit and solves for the OPTIMAL LEAD TIME TO TRIGGER ACTION as a function of forecast quality and of the operational characteristics (duration/effectiveness) of the action; the action is a generic flood preparedness measure, not a responder round trip, and 'latency' means forecast lead time, not observation-to-product delay.

title: Probabilistic short-range forecasts of high-precipitation events: optimal decision thresholds and predictability limits
authors: Bouttier, Francois; Marchal, Hugo
venue: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
one_line_difference: Optimises the probability decision threshold per user type AND reports the usable-intensity/scale limit beyond which the warning has no skill - i.e. an explicit skill boundary with a tuned threshold; the comparator is a deterministic control forecast, and the decision is a categorical warning, not a protective-action mission.

title: On the Relationship between the Quality and Value of Forecasts in the Generalized Cost-Loss Ratio Situation
authors: Chen, Yin-Sheng; Ehrendorfer, Martin; Murphy, Allan H.
one_line_difference: Extends the quality-value (non-)monotonicity result to the generalized N-action cost-loss situation; still no spatial hazard field, no mission- feasibility decision, no wildfire instantiation.

title: Conformal Risk Control for Safety-Critical Wildfire Evacuation Mapping: A Comparative Study of Tabular, Spatial, and Graph-Based Models
authors: Baljinnyam Dayan
one_line_difference: Shows directly that a high-AUROC fire-spread model is not thereby operationally adequate - standard thresholds captured only 7-72% of actual spread - and repairs it with conformal SAFE/MONITOR/EVACUATE zones at a bounded false-negative rate; it maps accuracy to a coverage guarantee, not to the timing of a protective action.

title: WUIVAC: a wildland-urban interface evacuation trigger model applied in strategic wildfire scenarios
authors: Philip E. Dennison; Thomas J. Cova; Max A. Moritz
one_line_difference: Turns the trigger buffer into a strategic planning product using 8 years of worst-case winds in 16 directions, including buffers for closure of evacuation routes; still deterministic, still egress-only, no responders.

title: A goal programming model for early evacuation of vulnerable people and relief distribution during a wildfire
authors: Inmaculada Flores; M. Teresa Ortuno; Gregorio Tirado
one_line_difference: Mixed-integer goal programming over a dynamic network of unsafe pick-up points and safe shelters/hospitals with heterogeneous vehicles and health-priority classes, case-studied on the 2019 Saddleridge fire — it owns the 'who gets fetched, by which vehicle, to where' question, with no fire-spread model and no deadline output.

title: Determinants of evacuation timing in response to probabilistic forecasts
authors: Georgakakos; Konstantine P.
one_line_difference: Solves 'issue the evacuation statement now vs delay' by Monte Carlo under a forecast probability sequence indexed by lead time, forecast uncertainty, public-response probability and the evacuation-completion time interval; hazard is generic and the completion interval is an exogenous scalar, not a modelled responder ingress+pickup+egress round trip against a spatial fire field.

title: k-PERIL: probabilistic creation of trigger boundaries for rural communities evacuating from a wildfire
authors: Nikolaos Kalogeropoulos; Harry Mitchell; Guillermo Rein
one_line_difference: Conference-proceedings first announcement of k-PERIL's probabilistic trigger boundaries; it is a conference book chapter, NOT a journal article, and must never be cited as one.

title: An Integrated Optimization for Resilient Wildfire Evacuation System Design: A Case Study of a Rural County in Korea
authors: Kyubin Kwon; Yejin Kim; Jinil Han
one_line_difference: Strategic mixed-integer shelter-location and backup-linkage design for a rural Korean county using static topographic/environmental wildfire risk indices; it does not model fire progression in time, and produces a network plan rather than any time-of-day decision, let alone a responder dispatch deadline.

title: Evaluating dynamic wildfire evacuation trigger buffers using the 2003 Cedar Fire
authors: Jeremy C. Larsen; Philip E. Dennison; Thomas J. Cova; Charles Jones
one_line_difference: First use of FORECAST winds (not climatology) to make trigger buffers dynamic, and the first retrospective validation of a trigger buffer against a real fire front; it does not quantify forecast skill or latency as decision variables.

title: A household-level approach to staging wildfire evacuation warnings using trigger modeling
authors: Dapeng Li; Thomas J. Cova; Philip E. Dennison
one_line_difference: Computes a trigger buffer PER HOUSEHOLD and ranks households by available lead time to stage warnings — the household-resolution and prioritisation-by-lead-time moves WildfireGuardian would otherwise claim; it does not model who physically moves the household.

title: Decision-Focused Learning: When and Why Traditional Prediction Models Fail
authors: Liu; Mo
one_line_difference: Tutorial stating flatly that improved predictive accuracy does not in general translate into improved decision quality, and that uncertainty- driven data collection is the wrong criterion in decision-focused settings - which pre-empts BOTH the WG-C-014 headline and the WG-C-008 motivation in generic form.

title: Bridging forecast verification and humanitarian decisions: A valuation approach for setting up action-oriented early warnings
authors: Lopez, Ana; Coughlan de Perez, Erin; Bazo, Juan; Suarez, Pablo; van den Hurk, Bart; van Aalst, Maarten
one_line_difference: Selects the joint (magnitude, probability threshold, lead time) that should trigger humanitarian action by valuation - i.e. a three-axis trigger boundary in forecast-quality space; the comparator is acting on climatology/no-action, and the triggered action has no mission-feasibility constraint.

title: Macroscopic Traffic Flow Network Modeling For Wildfire Evacuation: A Game-Theoretic Junction Optimization Approach with Application to Lahaina Fire
authors: Annie Lu; Hong Kiat Tan; Alexander Xue; Alice Koniges; Andrea L. Bertozzi
one_line_difference: Shows a lane can be RESERVED for emergency vehicles entering the network with negligible cost to civilian clearance time — it prices responder ingress against outbound flow at the network level, but never computes when a responder must leave.

title: Analyzing wildfire evacuation dynamics with agent-based modeling in damaged road networks
authors: Fangjiao Ma; Ji Yun Lee
one_line_difference: Couples wildfire simulation to road-network vulnerability so that fire-induced closures degrade the network during the evacuation and can trap agents — the 'network fails under the fire you predicted' mechanism WG-C-003 needs on its inbound leg, but applied only to outbound evacuees.

title: Value-of-information in spatio-temporal systems: Sensor placement and scheduling
authors: Malings, C.; Pozzi, M.
one_line_difference: Adds WHEN to sense (scheduling) to VOI-optimal WHERE, over a management time horizon; the temporal structure is system ageing, not a hard mission deadline against an advancing hazard.

title: Integrating wildfire spread and evacuation times to design safe triggers: Application to two rural communities using PERIL model
authors: Harry Mitchell; Steve Gwynne; Enrico Ronchi; Nikolaos Kalogeropoulos; Guillermo Rein
one_line_difference: Re-founds the trigger boundary in the fire-safety-engineering tradition (FARSITE + explicit safety factors for uncertainty) and validates on Swinley Forest UK and Roxborough Park USA; the safety factor is a margin, not a probability distribution, and there is no responder leg.

title: Government to improve the resident evacuation system in preparation for ultra-fast wildfires [translation]
authors: Ministry of the Interior and Safety (행정안전부), Social Disaster Response Coordination Division; jointly with Korea Forest Service (산림청)
one_line_difference: MOIS/KFS set two administratively fixed fire-arrival lead times (5 h general, 8 h vulnerable) as evacuation triggers from a deterministic spread forecast; WildfireGuardian computes a mission-feasibility dispatch deadline from an ensemble arrival-time distribution, and treats a fixed lead time like this one as the tuned comparator to beat.

title: AI-based wildfire and smoke spread monitoring and prediction [translation]
authors: Korea Forest Service (산림청); under a programme coordinated by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety (행정안전부)
one_line_difference: This programme outputs inbound suppression-ingress ROUTES alongside resident evacuation routes from an AI spread/smoke forecast; WildfireGuardian outputs a latest-safe DISPATCH TIME for an assisted-evacuation round trip. Same inbound leg, different decision variable — and this is a live Korean government programme, so WG-C-003 must be phrased as a quantity claim, never as a "no one does inbound routing in Korea" claim.

title: On the Relationship between the Accuracy and Value of Forecasts in the Cost-Loss Ratio Situation
authors: Murphy, Allan H.; Ehrendorfer, Martin
one_line_difference: Establishes in general terms that forecast accuracy and forecast value are not monotonically related in the cost-loss situation; it does so for scalar accuracy measures of binary forecasts, not for spatial overlap metrics (IoU) of a predicted fire perimeter against an evacuation-mission decision.

title: MORA: A Multicriteria Optimal Resource Allocation and Decision Support Toolkit for Wildfire Management
authors: Theofanis Orphanoudakis; Christos Betzelos; Helen Catherine Leligou
one_line_difference: Operational multicriteria resource-allocation DSS for incident commanders (SILVANUS project) allocating suppression resources; the allocated units are suppression assets, the objective is multicriteria fire management, and no resident-collection round trip or latest-dispatch time is computed.

title: Adaptive Monitoring of Stochastic Fire Front Processes via Information-seeking Predictive Control
authors: Savvas Papaioannou; Panayiotis Kolios; Christos G. Panayiotou; Marios M. Polycarpou
one_line_difference: The closest wildfire-specific prior art to WG-C-008: a drone trajectory chosen by information-seeking predictive control over a stochastic elliptical fire-front model, where the quantity optimised is estimation uncertainty and no protective-action deadline enters the objective.

title: A stochastic optimization model for staged hospital evacuation during hurricanes
authors: Tarun Rambha; Linda K. Nozick; Rachel Davidson; Wenqi Yi; Kun Yang
venue: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review
one_line_difference: Rambha et al. answer "in what order and at which forecast stage should patients be moved", producing an adaptive evacuate/shelter policy over a hurricane scenario tree; WildfireGuardian asks the inverse, closed-form question -- the single latest departure instant at which one responder's full round trip still closes under a modelled fire.

title: Stochastic decision trigger modelling to assess the probability of wildland fire impact
authors: J. Ramirez; S. Monedero; C. A. Silva; A. Cardil
one_line_difference: Produces a probability-of-arrival map for evacuation trigger buffers by perturbing fire-model inputs n times and states it can be solved in real time with any empirical propagation engine; the probabilistic trigger buffer as a deliverable is therefore already occupied, though the output remains a buffer and not a dispatch time.

title: A Dynamic Decision Model Applied to Hurricane Landfall
authors: Regnier, Eva; Harr, Patrick A.
one_line_difference: Owns 'act now vs wait for a better forecast' as a sequential decision problem where forecast accuracy is an explicit function of lead time; the protective action is an irreversible preparation cost, not a responder round trip with a mission-completion deadline.

title: Public Evacuation Decisions and Hurricane Track Uncertainty
authors: Regnier; Eva
one_line_difference: Computes, per location, the false-alarm rate forced by a required miss- probability given track-uncertainty-vs-lead-time, i.e. a forecast-quality boundary for evacuation ordering; the hazard is a hurricane track, the evacuation is an aggregate clearance time, and there is no responder- inclusive mission or tuned positional-trigger comparator.

title: Optimal Planning and Machine Learning for Responsive Tracking and Enhanced Forecasting of Wildfires using a Spacecraft Constellation
authors: Sreeja Roy-Singh; Vinay Ravindra; Richard Levinson; Mahta Moghaddam; Jan Mandel; Adam Kochanski; Angel Farguell Caus; Kurtis Nelson; Samira Alkaee Taleghan; Archana Kannan; Amer Melebari
one_line_difference: Schedules a satellite constellation for wildfire observation with a mixed-integer program and states an explicit end-to-end latency budget of 6-30 h; the objective maximises aggregate science reward with active-fire targets weighted ten-fold, which is a priority heuristic, not a downstream protective-action consequence.

title: Robust stochastic vehicle routing and scheduling for bushfire emergency evacuation: An Australian case study
authors: Shahrooz Shahparvari; Babak Abbasi
venue: Transportation Research Part A: Policy and Practice
one_line_difference: Last-mile, short-notice bushfire evacuation of late evacuees by capacitated vehicles under HARD TIME WINDOWS and route disruption, robustly optimised, on Black Saturday data — the oldest and strongest occupation of 'fetch people before the fire arrives', still with no fire-spread-derived deadline as the reported quantity.

title: Belief-Aware Scheduling for Predictive Wildfire Hazard Mapping under Sparse-Window Telemetry
authors: Shao, Xun; Yamakawa, Kohsuke; Cheah, Wai Shiang
one_line_difference: Wildfire active sensing: schedules sensing/representation/transmission under a sparse downlink so the receiver can predict an H-step-ahead hazard map; the objective is PREDICTIVE loss on the hazard map, not a protective-action decision loss, and the evaluation is a physics-calibrated synthetic environment with no evacuation decision.

title: Strategizing equitable transit evacuations: A data-driven reinforcement learning approach
authors: Fang Tang; Han Wang; Maria Laura Delle Monache
venue: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
one_line_difference: Transit vehicles must drive INTO the hazard area to collect carless/transit-dependent evacuees and drive them out, with RL allocating scarce vehicles — structurally the same base-pickup-destination trip as WG-C-003, but the control output is a dispatch POLICY, not a fire-relative latest-dispatch TIME, and fire arrival is not the binding constraint.

title: The simulation of wildland-urban interface fire evacuation: The WUI-NITY platform
authors: Jonathan Wahlqvist; Enrico Ronchi; Steven M.V. Gwynne; Max Kinateder; Guillermo Rein; Harry Mitchell; Noureddine Benichou; Chunyun Ma; Amanda Kimball; Erica Kuligowski
one_line_difference: The reference three-layer coupling (FARSITE fire + pedestrian + LWR traffic) with PERIL trigger buffers embedded, i.e. exactly the 'model future fire to inform evacuation' architecture WG-C-001 wrongly claimed as first; all traffic is outbound.

title: Forest Fire Spread Prediction and Assimilation Using the Deterministic Ensemble Kalman Filter
authors: Tianyu Wu; Qixing Zhang; Jiping Zhu; Liuheng Xu; Yongming Zhang
one_line_difference: Uses Observing System Simulation Experiments by name to validate a deterministic EnKF for fire-front correction, so OSSE is already a normal, named method inside wildfire spread prediction; its OSSE evaluates forecast accuracy, never an evacuation decision.

title: Disruption of emergency response to vulnerable populations during floods
authors: Dapeng Yu; Jie Yin; Robert L. Wilby; Stuart N. Lane; Jeroen C. J. H. Aerts; Ning Lin; Min Liu; Hongyong Yuan; Jianguo Chen; Christel Prudhomme; Mingfu Guan; Avinoam Baruch; C. W. D. Johnson; Xi Tang; Lizhong Yu; Shiyuan Xu
one_line_difference: Yu et al. model the inbound responder leg under a modelled hazard for exactly the vulnerable sites WildfireGuardian cares about, but they check arrival against an externally fixed response-time standard and never model pickup, egress, or a latest-dispatch time; the mission ends at arrival.

title: The distributed strategy for asynchronous observations in data-driven wildland fire spread prediction
authors: Mengxia Zha; Zheng Wang; Jie Ji; Jiping Zhu
one_line_difference: Runs OSSEs to generate asynchronous fire-front observations, treats observation staleness (latency) as the central problem, and concludes that observation resources should be concentrated where spread rates are highest; the allocation rule is driven by prediction error, not by any protective-action consequence.

title: Vehicle routing and scheduling for bushfire emergency evacuation
authors: Babak Abbasi; Shahrooz Shahparvari; Prem Chhetri
venue: 2015 IEEE International Conference on Industrial Engineering and Engineering Management (IEEM)
one_line_difference: Earliest paper in the Shahparvari/Abbasi bushfire-VRP lineage; determines vehicles, schedules and routes inside given time windows and fire-propagation scenarios, with no deadline as output.

title: Generation and evaluation of an ensemble of wildland fire simulations
authors: Frederic Allaire; Jean-Baptiste Filippi; Vivien Mallet
one_line_difference: Imports meteorological probabilistic verification (burn-probability maps scored with proper scores) into wildfire, on seven real Corsican fires; it scores the forecast, never the decision, and its ensemble is single-model Monte Carlo over inputs.

title: Analysis of Evacuation Behavior among Disaster-Vulnerable Groups during Wildfire Events Using Mobile Floating Population Data: A Case Study of the 2022 Mangsang and Mukho-dong, Donghae
authors: Korea Safety Culture Society
venue: Forum of Public Safety and Culture
one_line_difference: Measures OBSERVED Korean evacuation response time and movement intensity by population group after a real disaster text message (2022 Donghae fire), finding older adults had the lowest movement intensity; it measures behaviour, it does not compute any deadline. Its finding is the strongest empirical Korean support for the premise behind WG-C-005.

title: Real-time wildfire monitoring with a fleet of UAVs
authors: Rafael Bailon-Ruiz; Arthur Bit-Monnot; Simon Lacroix
one_line_difference: Closes the loop the other way round from most sensing work - a fire-spread forecast defines where the UAV fleet should look next - but the observation plan is scored by coverage of the predicted fire perimeter, never by what a commander would do differently.

title: Partitioned Iterative Quantum Scheduling of Satellites for Urgent Disaster Response: Case study of Wildfire
authors: Lucas T. Braydwood; Taejin Park; Hirofumi Hashimoto; Zoe Gonzalez Izquierdo; Andrew Michaelis; Eleanor Rieffel; Shon Grabbe
one_line_difference: Satellite tasking for urgent wildfire response solved with iterative quantum algorithms; the objective is scheduling efficiency and near-real-time coverage, with no link from a scheduling choice to an evacuation or dispatch consequence.

title: Stochastic ambulance dispatching and routing in mass casualty incident under road vulnerability
authors: Kuo-Hao Chang
venue: Journal of the Operational Research Society
one_line_difference: The scarce-ambulance allocation formulation WG-C-011 would occupy, solved for survivor count rather than for a dispatch time.

title: Multiscale Wildfire-Evacuation Modeling: Assessing Differential Access to Safe Egress in Marin County, CA
authors: Saemi Chang; Louise Comfort; Kenichi Soga; Pengshun Li; Yanglan Wang
one_line_difference: Chang et al. show that ALERT LATENCY and mobility constraints jointly determine who gets out -- the nearest published treatment of latency as a decision-relevant variable in wildfire evacuation -- but for self-evacuating households, with no responder, no pickup, and no deadline. This is the closest existing work to WG-C-012's spirit inside Category 9.

title: Modeling Evacuate versus Shelter-in-Place Decisions in Wildfires
authors: Thomas J. Cova; Philip E. Dennison; Frank A. Drews
one_line_difference: Poses wildfire protective action as an explicit decision-analytic choice (evacuate vs shelter-in-place) with a loss structure, which is the decision-theoretic framing WG-C-002 builds on; it does not parameterise the decision by forecast skill, lead time or latency.

title: Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem Under Deadlines: An Application to Flooding Crisis
authors: Florent Dubois; Paul Renaud-Goud; Patricia Stolf
one_line_difference: A useful precedent for the phrase "deadline" in rescue routing, but the deadlines are exogenous per-victim constraints; nothing is computed backwards from a hazard-progression model.

title: An optimization model for evacuating people with disability in extreme disaster conditions: A case study
authors: Sadoullah Ebrahimnejad; Michelle Villeneuve; Reza Tavakkoli-Moghaddam
volume: UNVERIFIED # Crossref returned volume 0, issue 0, pages 0-0 (article in press record)
one_line_difference: NEEDS_FULL_TEXT -- recorded from bibliographic metadata only.

title: Supported Evacuation for Disaster Relief through Lexicographic Goal Programming
authors: Inmaculada Flores; M. Teresa Ortuno; Gregorio Tirado; Begona Vitoriano
one_line_difference: Establishes the term and the model class 'supported evacuation' (health-condition classes, dynamic arrival at pick-up points, no trade-off between objectives) on an earthquake/tsunami case — the framing WG-C-005 must cite rather than claim.

title: Wildland firefighter entrapment avoidance: modelling evacuation triggers
authors: Gregory K. Fryer; Philip E. Dennison; Thomas J. Cova
one_line_difference: Moves the trigger subject from residents to FIREFIGHTERS and varies the evacuation MODE (foot, engine, dozer), which is the closest the classical lineage gets to a responder — but the responder's modelled leg is still one-way egress to a safety zone, never an inbound round trip.

title: Fast-moving dire wildfire evacuation simulation
authors: Sarah Grajdura; Sachraa Borjigin; Deb Niemeier
venue: Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment
one_line_difference: Establishes empirically that reduced vehicle access plus notification delay is what traps people in a fast-moving fire -- the motivating evidence for WG-C-003 -- while explicitly not modelling any assistance being sent.

title: Roxborough Park Community Wildfire Evacuation Drill: Data Collection and Model Benchmarking
authors: Steve M. V. Gwynne; Enrico Ronchi; Jonathan Wahlqvist; Arturo Cuesta; Javier Gonzalez Villa; Erica D. Kuligowski; Amanda Kimball; Guillermo Rein; Max Kinateder; Noureddine Benichou; Hui Xie
one_line_difference: Supplies the real community-drill dataset (departure and arrival times) that both the trigger lineage and the supported-evacuation OR lineage now benchmark against — it is the empirical baseline WG-C-006 must beat or at least match.

title: A cost-benefit analysis of WildFireSat, a wildfire monitoring satellite mission for Canada
authors: Hope, Emily S.; McKenney, Daniel W.; Johnston, Lynn M.; Johnston, Joshua M.
one_line_difference: Values a wildfire OBSERVING SYSTEM as a whole by cost-benefit analysis; the unit of analysis is a mission programme, not the marginal decision value of an individual observation under a deadline.

title: Directional analysis of community wildfire evacuation capabilities
authors: Amy M. Kim; Jennifer L. Beverly; Abdullah Al Zahid
one_line_difference: Asks which DIRECTIONS of fire approach a community can and cannot evacuate against, which is close to WG-C-009 robust protectability, but the capability is an egress property of the community, not a mission-feasibility property of a responder.

title: Development of Evacuation Route Planning Algorithm for Responding to Urban Forest Fires
authors: Kwak, Jae-Hwan (곽재환); Kim, Namgyun (김남균); Kim, Man-Il (김만일)
venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Hazard Mitigation / 한국방재학회논문집
one_line_difference: Kwak et al. enumerate up to fifteen GIS shortest-path evacuation routes per origin to a shelter under an urban-wildfire spread zone; the output is a route set with no departure time, no time-varying fire front, and no responder leg.

title: Decision-oriented benchmarking to transform AI weather forecast access: Application to the Indian monsoon
authors: Masiwal, Rajat; Aitken, Colin; Marchakitus, Adam; Gupta, Mayank; Kowal, Katherine; Pahlavan, Hamid A.; Yang, Tyler; Sun, Y. Qiang; Kremer, Michael; Jina, Amir; Boos, William R.; Hassanzadeh, Pedram
one_line_difference: Builds a decision-oriented benchmark (miss rate, false alarm rate, skill vs climatology, operational runnability) to choose which forecast system to deploy; the comparator is climatology, the decision is agricultural planting, and operational latency is a selection criterion but is not a quantified decision variable.

title: A robust optimisation approach for the placement of forest fire suppression resources
authors: Andre Bergsten Mendes; Filipe Pereira e Alvelos
one_line_difference: Robust initial-attack placement of suppression resources against uncertain predicted fire behaviour; robustness is over fire-behaviour uncertainty for asset positioning, not over whether a named resident remains extractable, and the decision is placement, not dispatch timing.

title: Development of an Evacuation System for Reducing Damages by Forest Disaster
authors: Yoon, Ho-joong (윤호중) [principal investigator]; National Institute of Forest Science (국립산림과학원)
venue: Research report to the Korea Forest Service (산림청); NTIS/ScienceON report TRKO201800042755
one_line_difference: NIFoS computes an evacuation RANGE (which area must clear) from modelled smoke dispersion and ranks warning-evacuation priority; WildfireGuardian computes an evacuation TIME (when a responder must depart) from modelled fire-front arrival on both legs of a round trip.

title: Assessing the real-world economic value of weather forecasts for compounding extremes
authors: Olivetti, Leonardo; Messori, Gabriele; Avner, Paolo; Hallegatte, Stephane
one_line_difference: Shows model rankings flip with cost-loss ratio and penalty structure (IFS HRES vs AIFS), i.e. meteorological skill does not determine which system is better for a given decision-maker; urban multi-hazard, no evacuation mission.

title: Participatory multi-criteria decision analysis to prioritize management areas that help suppress wildfires
authors: Sergio Rodriguez-Fernandez; Philip J. Murphy; Keith M. Reynolds; Srijana Poudel; Jose Ramon Gonzalez-Olabarria; Jose G. Borges
venue: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
one_line_difference: Spatial prioritisation of fuel-management areas using stakeholder-weighted MCDA in Portugal; ranks landscape units for pre-season treatment, not interventions ranked by their effect on an individual mission's feasibility.

title: A Simulation-Based Framework for Leveraging Shared Autonomous Vehicles to Enhance Disaster Evacuations in Rural Regions with a Focus on Vulnerable Populations
authors: Sevim, Alican; Guo, Qian-wen; Ozguven, Eren Erman
one_line_difference: PROVISIONAL RECORD. The rural + vulnerable + dispatched-vehicle combination is the closest demographic match to the Korean setting; its treatment of "timing" must be read in full before WG-C-003 or WG-C-011 is defended.

title: Enhancing emergency evacuation response of late evacuees: Revisiting the case of Australian Black Saturday bushfire
authors: Shahrooz Shahparvari; Prem Chhetri; Babak Abbasi; Ahmad Abareshi
venue: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review
one_line_difference: Multi-objective tactical plan for clearing late evacuees inside a hard time window; the reported result is feasibility of the plan, not the latest time at which dispatch would still have been feasible.

title: Possibilistic scheduling routing for short-notice bushfire emergency evacuation under uncertainties: An Australian case study
authors: Shahrooz Shahparvari; Babak Abbasi; Prem Chhetri
one_line_difference: NEEDS_FULL_TEXT -- recorded from bibliographic metadata only; no abstract retrieved.

title: Fleet routing and scheduling in bushfire emergency evacuation: A regional case study of the Black Saturday bushfires in Australia
authors: Shahparvari; Abbasi; Chhetri; Abareshi
venue: Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment
one_line_difference: Regional fleet routing/scheduling for bushfire evacuation; recorded for completeness of the Shahparvari lineage - NEEDS_FULL_TEXT before it is cited, since only a truncated Crossref title and family names were verified.

title: An interdisciplinary agent-based multimodal wildfire evacuation model: Critical decisions and life safety
authors: M.R.K. Siam; Haizhong Wang; Michael K. Lindell; Chen Chen; Eleni I. Vlahogianni; Kay Axhausen
venue: Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment
one_line_difference: Multimodal agent-based wildfire evacuation tying household decision timing to life-safety outcomes; establishes that 'critical decisions' are the right output unit, but the decision is the household's departure, not a responder's dispatch.

title: The Costs and Costs Avoided From Wildfire Fire Management - A Conceptual Framework for a Value of Information Analysis
authors: Simon, Benjamin; Crowley, Christopher; Franco, Fabiano
one_line_difference: Wildfire VOI exists, but as a CONCEPTUAL cost-minimisation framework over fuel treatment / suppression / rehabilitation effort; explicitly does not address sensor selection, observation timing, or decision-directed sensing.

title: The Economic Value of Forecasts in Reducing Extreme Total Losses
authors: Stephenson; David B.
one_line_difference: Derives expected loss and loss VARIANCE as functions of hit rate and false alarm rate, showing the minimum-VaR operating point differs from the minimum-expected-loss point - another accuracy/value non-alignment result, in closed form, hazard-generic.

title: Real-Time Wildfire Monitoring via Geostationary Satellite and Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the March 2025 South Korea Wildfires
authors: Sung, Taejun; Lee, Garyung; Kim, Doeun; Kim, Woohyeok; Yang, Seyoung; Im, Jungho
venue: Korean Journal of Remote Sensing / 한국원격탐사학회지
one_line_difference: Quantifies Korean wildfire OBSERVATION latency (mean 12.9-18.2 min geostationary vs 210-318 min polar-orbiting; Uiseong detected in 22-36 min vs 93-196 min) but never converts latency into decision value. WG-C-012 needs exactly this number as an input and must cite it rather than re-derive it.

title: Estimating the benefits of single value and probability forecasting for flood warning
authors: Verkade, J. S.; Werner, M. G. F.
one_line_difference: Computes REV of deterministic vs probabilistic flood forecasts as a function of lead time with a no-warning/perfect-warning reference; no tuned positional trigger, no mission deadline.

title: Multi-Parking Lot and Shelter Heterogeneous Vehicle Routing Problem With Split Pickup Under Emergencies
authors: Lina Xu; Ziyang Wang; Xudong Chen; Zhengwei Lin
one_line_difference: Owns the "who gets which vehicle" matching constraint (mobility class to vehicle class) that WG-C-011 would otherwise claim, but with no hazard progression and no timing feasibility at all.

title: Does Your Wildfire Prediction Model Actually Work, or Just Score Well?
authors: Xu, Yangshuang; Dai, Yuyang; Chang, Liling; Wang, Qi; Dong, Yushun
one_line_difference: Shows wildfire model rankings flip with evaluation design (matching rules, head selection) under a fixed-contract framework; the sensitivity is metric- to-metric within prediction, NOT prediction-metric-to-decision-quality, so it does not itself occupy WG-C-014.

title: A round-trip bus evacuation model with scheduling and routing planning
authors: Xing Zhao; Kang Ji; Peng Xu; Wen-wen Qian; Gang Ren; Xiao-nian Shan
venue: Transportation Research Part A: Policy and Practice
one_line_difference: Owns the phrase "round-trip" in bus evacuation -- depot to pickup point to shelter and back, with bus capacity, demand and time-window constraints -- but minimises total evacuee time cost with no hazard progression and no departure deadline.

title: The Economic Value of Ensemble-Based Weather Forecasts
authors: Zhu, Yuejian; Toth, Zoltan; Wobus, Richard; Richardson, David; Mylne, Kenneth
venue: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
one_line_difference: Shows ensembles beat a higher-resolution control forecast across the cost- loss spectrum; the comparator is a competing forecast system, not a tuned non-forecast policy.

title: Evacuation Planning on Time-Expanded Networks with Integrated Wildfire Information
authors: Steffen Borgwardt; Nicholas Crawford; Drew Horton; Angela Morrison; Emily Speakman
one_line_difference: Uses a predicted fire to build and then update a self-evacuation flow plan; contains no assisted evacuation, no responder and no deadline. Relevant to WG-C-001/002, not to WG-C-003.

title: Wildfire Perimeters Align with Topographic Ridge Lines: A Null Model Benchmark for Fire-Spread Modelling in 118 Korean Wildfires (2018-2025)
authors: Choi, J. H.; Chae, HeeMun
one_line_difference: Establishes a Korea-specific observational benchmark (fire perimeters are ridge-proximal AND ridge-aligned, mean enrichment 2.3 vs 1.5 for proximity alone) against which a fire-spread model must be judged in Korea. This is the single best candidate evidence for a NOVELTY_STANDARD §4(a)/(b) argument, because it gives a documented Korean terrain signal that a spread model can be shown to reproduce or miss.

title: Demand for Information for Wildland Fire Management
authors: Frisvold, George B.; Zhang, Ning; Crimmins, Michael A.; Ferguson, Daniel; Maxwell, Charles
one_line_difference: Empirical study of WHO uses fire information and when; descriptive demand- side evidence, no normative VOI computation and no sensing design.

title: Prediction of Wildfire Spread and Propagation Algorithm for Disaster Area
authors: Gu, Nam-kyung (구남경); Lee, Kang-hwan (이강환)
venue: Journal of the Korea Institute of Information and Communication Engineering / 한국정보통신학회논문지
one_line_difference: A sensor-network spread-direction/speed predictor whose abstract says the result could tell nearby residents whether and by when to evacuate; the paper reports a prediction algorithm, not any computed evacuation deadline. Claim only what the abstract supports (evidence level E2 — abstract only).

title: A Comparative Review of Wildfire Danger Rating Systems: Focus on Fuel Moisture Modeling Frameworks
authors: Han, Songhee; Heo, Sujung; Lee, Yeeun; Jang, Mina; Jung, Sungcheol; Ahn, Sujung
one_line_difference: Peer-reviewed characterisation of the Korean KFDRS against NFDRS/CFFDRS/EFFIS/AFDRS, documenting that KFDRS is daily, district-resolution, empirical and weather-driven with no live-fuel-moisture model. This is a citable, independent statement of a Korean operational limitation — useful raw material for a §4(b) argument.

title: Bridging Climate and Socio-Environmental Vulnerability for Wildfire Risk Assessment Using Explainable Machine Learning: Evidence from the 2025 Wildfire in Korea
authors: Heo, Sujung; Ahn, Sujung; Lee, Ye-Eun; Jung, Sung-Cheol; Jang, Mina
one_line_difference: Maps 2025-fire susceptibility against socio-environmental exposure in Gyeongbuk (CatBoost/LightGBM, AUC ~0.91), reporting that high-susceptibility corridors coincide with counties of high elderly share; it is a static risk map, not a timing analysis.

title: Traffic Performance Indicators for Evacuation: The Case Study of the 2020 Silverado Wildfire
authors: Nima Janfeshanaraghi; Arthur Rohaert; Enrico Ronchi; Noureddine Benichou; Erica D. Kuligowski
one_line_difference: Defines empirical traffic performance indicators from a real wildfire evacuation, giving the field measured comparators; useful as a source of realistic congestion numbers for WG-C-003's ingress leg, not a competing claim.

title: Using reverse geocoding to identify prominent wildfire evacuation trigger points
authors: Dapeng Li; Thomas J. Cova; Philip E. Dennison
one_line_difference: Operationalises trigger buffers into named landmarks a dispatcher can say out loud; purely a communicability step, no decision-quantity novelty.

title: Playing the long game: Anticipatory action based on seasonal forecasts
authors: MacLeod, David; Kniveton, Dominic R.; Todd, Martin C.
one_line_difference: Asks how long a forecast-based-action system must run before value is realised with confidence; a temporal-sampling question, not a skill-boundary question.

title: National Forest Fire Danger Forecasting System [translation]
authors: National Institute of Forest Science (국립산림과학원); Forest Disaster Prediction and Analysis Center (산림재난예측분석센터)
venue: Operational national system, forestfire.nifos.go.kr; statutory basis 산림보호법 제31조 및 시행령 제23조
one_line_difference: KFDRS issues a 1–100 ignition-danger index from weather, terrain and forest type (임상); it says nothing about when anyone should leave. It is an input layer, not an evacuation decision tool.

title: Social Vulnerabilities and Wildfire Evacuations: A Case Study of the 2019 Kincade Fire
authors: Sun, Yuran; Forrister, Ana; Kuligowski, Erica D.; Lovreglio, Ruggiero; Cova, Thomas J.; Zhao, Xilei
one_line_difference: PROVISIONAL RECORD. Empirical evidence on differential wildfire evacuation outcomes for vulnerable groups; no model of assistance provision.

title: Does Your Wildfire Prediction Model Actually Work, or Just Score Well?
one_line_difference: Shows 'selection regret' between PR-AUC and decision-F1 for wildfire occupancy/spread tasks; it is a classification-metric result, not an evacuation-deadline result. PREPRINT.

title: Emulation of wildland fire spread simulation using deep learning
authors: Frederic Allaire; Vivien Mallet; Jean-Baptiste Filippi
one_line_difference: Quantifies the emulation trade WildfireGuardian depends on: a several-thousand-fold speed-up bought at a burned-area MAPE of 32.8%; it reports that error as an approximation cost, not as a decision cost.

title: The Rothermel surface fire spread model and associated developments: A comprehensive explanation
authors: Patricia L. Andrews
venue: USDA Forest Service, Rocky Mountain Research Station, General Technical Report RMRS-GTR-371
one_line_difference: Reference consolidation of the Rothermel equations and their NFDRS/BEHAVE variants; it is the document that tells us which Rothermel variant a downstream simulator actually implements, and nothing about decisions.

title: Observing-Systems Simulation Experiments: Past, Present, and Future
venue: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
one_line_difference: Foundational OSSE methodology statement, including the identical-twin problem. NEEDS_FULL_TEXT to quote directly.

title: Atmospheric Observations and Experiments to Assess Their Usefulness in Data Assimilation
venue: Journal of the Meteorological Society of Japan. Ser. II
one_line_difference: Classic statement of OSSE validation requirements in NWP. NEEDS_FULL_TEXT: cited secondhand via Yu et al. 2019 for the identical-twin bias claim.

title: Accounting for emergency response in building evacuation
authors: Jason D. Averill; Weiguo Song
one_line_difference: Building-fire, not wildfire: models first responders moving UP a stairwell against occupants moving down, i.e. the counterflow ingress penalty - the mechanism WG-C-003 needs, established decades ago in a different hazard and at a different scale; it is a government report, NOT peer-reviewed.

title: Aligning simulation models: A case study and results
one_line_difference: Introduces docking (model-to-model alignment) as the evidence standard when two models are supposed to represent the same system.

title: Assessment of fire spread predictions from the Wildfire Intelligence and Simulation Engine (W.I.S.E.) using a large set of satellite-derived wildfire perimeters
authors: L. Bennett; P. Jain; B. Moore; J. Boisvert
one_line_difference: The largest published spatial-agreement evaluation of an operational national fire growth model (19,848 fire-days, default-parameter IoU 0.194); it measures perimeter accuracy and explicitly does not connect that accuracy to any decision outcome, which is the gap WG-C-014 targets.

title: Planning for a bus-based evacuation
authors: Douglas R. Bish
one_line_difference: The canonical bus-based-evacuation formulation for carless populations. Note the design feature closest to WG-C-003: the last pickup at each location is required to occur by a location-specific, risk-determined time -- an exogenous location deadline, not one derived from a modelled hazard, and applied to the pickup instant rather than to dispatch.

title: Bootstrap-Based Improvements for Inference with Clustered Errors
one_line_difference: Gives the exact small-cluster correction our few-event design needs; an econometrics paper, no hazard content.

title: A Practitioner's Guide to Cluster-Robust Inference
one_line_difference: Survey giving the decision rules for choosing the clustering level; not hazard-specific.

title: Data-driven surrogate model with latent data assimilation: Application to wildfire forecasting
authors: Sibo Cheng; I. Colin Prentice; Yuhan Huang; Yufang Jin; Yi-Ke Guo; Rossella Arcucci
one_line_difference: Couples an LSTM reduced-order surrogate (about 1000x faster than the cellular-automata simulator it emulates) to latent data assimilation of daily satellite perimeters on three Californian fires; the assimilation cadence is daily, which is the latency constraint WG-C-012 is about, but the paper never treats latency as a decision variable.

title: Uncertainty associated with model predictions of surface and crown fire rates of spread
authors: Miguel G. Cruz; Martin E. Alexander
one_line_difference: The canonical synthesis of rate-of-spread prediction error across 49 datasets and 1278 observations; it establishes the error magnitudes WildfireGuardian's forecast-skill ranges must span, but says nothing about what those errors cost a decision-maker.

title: Are we really making much progress? A worrying analysis of recent neural recommendation approaches
venue: Proceedings of the 13th ACM Conference on Recommender Systems (RecSys '19)
one_line_difference: The canonical demonstration that weak/untuned baselines manufacture apparent progress; recommender systems, not hazards.

title: Smart 'Predict, then Optimize
one_line_difference: Establishes that prediction error and decision regret are different objectives; generic optimisation setting, no hazard or deadline content.

title: ELMFIRE documentation: Validation
authors: ELMFIRE Developers (C. Lautenberger et al.)
one_line_difference: The model's own documentation reports mean Jaccard 0.178 / Sorensen 0.278 for ELMFIRE and 0.176 / 0.274 for FARSITE against historic CONUS fires - the single cheapest citation for how wrong operational spread models are, and it is software documentation, not a peer-reviewed evaluation.

title: Development and validation of observing-system simulation experiments at NASA's Global Modeling and Assimilation Office
venue: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society
one_line_difference: Operational template for building and validating an OSSE system; NWP domain. NEEDS_FULL_TEXT.

title: FARSITE: Fire Area Simulator - model development and evaluation
authors: Mark A. Finney
venue: USDA Forest Service, Rocky Mountain Research Station, Research Paper RMRS-RP-4 (revised 2004)
one_line_difference: FARSITE is the deterministic Huygens-wavelet growth engine the trigger literature (Cova 2005, PERIL) runs; it is a government research paper documenting a simulator, not a study of decision quality.

title: The collection 6 MODIS active fire detection algorithm and fire products
authors: Louis Giglio; Wilfrid Schroeder; Christopher O. Justice
one_line_difference: The 1 km MODIS heritage product against which VIIRS and geostationary detectors are benchmarked; at 1 km it cannot resolve the fire-front geometry a trigger boundary needs.

title: Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
one_line_difference: Defines proper scoring and the calibration/sharpness decomposition our forecast-quality axis must use.

title: Geostationary active fire products validation: GOES-17 ABI, GOES-16 ABI, and Himawari AHI
authors: J. V. Hall; W. Schroeder; K. Rishmawi; M. Wooster; C. C. Schmidt; C. Huang; I. Csiszar; L. Giglio
one_line_difference: The reference validation of geostationary fire detection against simultaneous Landsat, giving both the cadence (10 min full disk, 5 min CONUS, 30-60 s mesoscale) and the geolocation penalty for steep terrain that WildfireGuardian must budget for in Korea.

title: Rigorous Evaluation of a Fraternal Twin Ocean OSSE System for the Open Gulf of Mexico
venue: Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology
one_line_difference: The clearest published statement of fraternal-twin design criteria and of the requirement that an OSSE neither over- nor under-estimates impact; ocean domain.

title: Inverse Crime' and Model Integrity in Lightcurve Inversion applied to unresolved Space Object Identification
venue: The Journal of the Astronautical Sciences
one_line_difference: Empirical demonstration that committing the inverse crime yields misleadingly optimistic parameter estimates; different domain (space object ID).

title: Future Observing System Simulation Experiments
venue: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
one_line_difference: Modern OSSE review and design guidance. NEEDS_FULL_TEXT: AMS site returned 403; metadata verified via Crossref only.

title: Pseudoreplication and the Design of Ecological Field Experiments
one_line_difference: Defines the unit-of-analysis error that our per-scenario statistics would commit; not about wildfire.

title: Statistical inverse problems: Discretization, model reduction and inverse crimes
venue: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
one_line_difference: Canonical peer-reviewed treatment of inverse crimes and the Bayesian approximation-error approach that repairs them. NEEDS_FULL_TEXT: abstract elided by publisher.

title: The Jackknife and the Bootstrap for General Stationary Observations
one_line_difference: Provides the block-resampling machinery for dependent sequences; says nothing about wildfire or decisions.

title: Equivalence Tests: A Practical Primer for t Tests, Correlations, and Meta-Analyses
one_line_difference: Supplies the TOST procedure and the SESOI requirement; not about forecasts or hazards.

title: Equivalence Testing for Psychological Research: A Tutorial
venue: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science
one_line_difference: The operational tutorial for TOST including how to set and justify the equivalence bound.

title: Wildland fire modeling with an Eulerian level set method and automated calibration
authors: Chris Lautenberger
one_line_difference: Defines ELMFIRE, the level-set spread engine with an MPI Monte Carlo mode that makes 1000-member operational ensembles affordable; it is a modelling paper, and its ensemble is over input uncertainty, not over decisions.

title: What exactly is 'N' in cell culture and animal experiments?
one_line_difference: Modern restatement of the unit-of-analysis error with a three-level unit taxonomy we can adopt verbatim.

title: Studying wildfire behavior using FIRETEC
authors: Rodman Linn; Jon Reisner; Jonah J. Colman; Judith Winterkamp
one_line_difference: The reference CFD-scale physical fire model; recorded so the review can state explicitly that WildfireGuardian does not and cannot use this class of model in decision time.

title: Recent advances and applications of WRF-SFIRE
authors: J. Mandel; S. Amram; J. D. Beezley; G. Kelman; A. K. Kochanski; V. Y. Kondratenko; B. H. Lynn; B. Regev; M. Vejmelka
venue: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
one_line_difference: The coupled atmosphere-fire model that makes fire-induced wind feedback available, and the one that assimilates satellite fire detections via fire-arrival-time; it is a physics/NWP contribution whose cost puts it outside decision-time ensemble use.

title: Decision-Focused Learning: Foundations, State of the Art, Benchmark and Future Opportunities
one_line_difference: Survey establishing that the prediction-metric vs decision-metric gap is a named, mature research area.

title: Evacuation and Transportation Barriers Among Vulnerable Populations in Natural Hazard-Related Disasters: A Scoping Review
authors: Yuriko Matsuo; Kathryn Kietzman; Ron D. Hays; Yeonsu Song
venue: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
one_line_difference: The best available synthesis of the EVIDENCE BASE for who cannot self-evacuate; contains no model, no optimisation and no timing quantity. WildfireGuardian should cite it to justify the population definition, never as prior art on the method.

title: SPARK - A Bushfire Spread Prediction Tool
authors: Claire Miller; James Hilton; Andrew Sullivan; Mahesh Prakash
venue: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology (Environmental Software Systems)
one_line_difference: GPU level-set spread tool (CSIRO) whose per-run cost is low enough for large ensembles; a simulator paper, with no decision quantity.

title: Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods
one_line_difference: Gives the reporting skeleton and the Monte Carlo standard error requirement our scenario counts must satisfy.

title: FIRMS ultra real-time, real-time and near real-time active fire data latency (NASA LANCE/FIRMS documentation)
authors: NASA LANCE FIRMS team
venue: NASA Earthdata FIRMS wiki / NASA Earthdata feature article
one_line_difference: The operator's own latency figures - under 60 s (direct readout, US/Canada only), 20-30 min real-time, about 3 h near-real-time - which set the floor on how stale WildfireGuardian's fire-position input can be, and show that the fast tier does not exist over Korea.

title: Verification, Validation, and Confirmation of Numerical Models in the Earth Sciences
one_line_difference: Philosophical constraint on what simulation evidence can establish; prohibits the word 'validated' for our OSSE.

title: Can You Trust Your Model's Uncertainty? Evaluating Predictive Uncertainty Under Dataset Shift
one_line_difference: Empirical demonstration that calibration degrades under shift and that post-hoc temperature scaling does not survive it; image/text benchmarks, not fire.

title: Leveraging MTG-FCI fire observations for event-based fire behavior monitoring from near-real-time operation to seasonal analysis
authors: Ronan Paugam; Jean-Baptiste Filippi; Akli Benali; Jorge Gomes; Weidong Xu; Emanuel Dutra; Francois Andre; Damien Boulanger; Vianney Retornard; Andrea Meraner; Julia Harvie; Victor Penot; Cyrielle Denjean
one_line_difference: Shows geostationary observation cadence being converted into an operationally updated rate-of-spread estimate every 10 minutes - the observed-quantity-to-inferred-quantity step WildfireGuardian depends on; spatial resolution and product latency are not stated in the retrievable abstract.

title: Robustness of Observing System Simulation Experiments
venue: Tellus A: Dynamic Meteorology and Oceanography
one_line_difference: Shows OSSE impact magnitudes shift with the amount of injected model error while spatial patterns stay stable; supplies the 'degree of twinning must be well understood' standard.

title: The verification of wildland-urban interface fire evacuation models
one_line_difference: Domain-specific verification protocol for WUI evacuation models including trigger buffers; verification only, no real-event validation.

title: A mathematical model for predicting fire spread in wildland fuels
authors: Richard C. Rothermel
venue: USDA Forest Service, Intermountain Forest and Range Experiment Station, Research Paper INT-RP-115
one_line_difference: Rothermel supplies the steady-state surface rate-of-spread kernel that WildfireGuardian's forecasts inherit; it is a government research paper, not a peer-reviewed article, and it computes spread rate, not any decision quantity.

title: Verification and validation of simulation models
one_line_difference: The standard V&V taxonomy for discrete-event/simulation models; domain-neutral.

title: The New VIIRS 375 m active fire detection data product: Algorithm description and initial assessment
authors: Wilfrid Schroeder; Patricia Oliva; Louis Giglio; Ivan A. Csiszar
one_line_difference: Defines the 375 m polar-orbiting active-fire product that is the default fire-position observation for most of the world; it produces detection points, not fire perimeters or rates of spread, and its revisit is the binding constraint WG-C-012 inherits.

title: Simulation studies for methodological research in psychology: A standardized template for planning, preregistration, and reporting
one_line_difference: Turns ADEMP into a preregistration template; the defence against accusations that the tuned baseline was chosen after seeing results.

title: Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift
one_line_difference: Gives the exact condition (known/estimable covariate-shift likelihood ratio) under which coverage survives; no hazard application.

title: Fire spread in chaparral - a comparison of laboratory data and model predictions in burning live fuels
authors: David R. Weise; Eunmo Koo; Xiangyang Zhou; Shankar Mahalingam; Frederic Morandini; Jacques-Henri Balbi
one_line_difference: Documents outright model failure rather than model error: with default values Rothermel failed to predict spread in nearly all 240 live-fuel chaparral fires, and the tested models were correct only 49-69% of the time.

title: Transparent reporting items for simulation studies evaluating statistical methods: Foundations for reproducibility and reliability
one_line_difference: Checklist of reporting items; ecology/evolution framing but domain-neutral content.

title: The inverse crime
one_line_difference: Short polemic giving the crisp definition we will quote; a preprint, never cite as a journal article.

title: Evaluation of nonidentical versus identical twin approaches for observation impact assessments: an ensemble-Kalman-filter-based ocean assimilation application for the Gulf of Mexico
one_line_difference: The citable quantitative demonstration that identical twins overestimate observation impact (45% vs 29% temperature-error reduction); ocean DA, not wildfire decisions.

title: Systematic review and research gaps on wildfire evacuations: infrastructure, transportation modes, networks, and planning
authors: Syeda Narmeen Zehra; Stephen D. Wong
one_line_difference: Review, not primary work. Its declared research gaps must be read in full before WildfireGuardian asserts any gap of its own, because a review that already names our gap converts our contribution from "unnoticed" to "known and open".

title: Use of Observing System Simulation Experiments in the United States
venue: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
one_line_difference: A NOAA SAB-derived review that lists 'extension of OSSEs to societal impacts' as an outstanding recommendation - i.e. the decision-level OSSE was an open item as of 2020.

title: Examining and Reforming the Rothermel Surface Fire Spread Model under No-Wind and Zero-Slope Conditions for the Karst Ecosystems
authors: Yunlin Zhang; Lingling Tian
one_line_difference: One of a family of East-Asian laboratory recalibration studies showing Rothermel relative error up to 50% on non-US fuels; it is the transfer-failure evidence WildfireGuardian needs to justify not assuming US-calibrated spread rates in Korea.

title: Spread Speed of Forest Fire based on Slope
authors: An, Sang-Hyun (안상현); Shin, Young-Chul (신영철)
venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Hazard Mitigation / 한국방재학회논문집
one_line_difference: Korean experimental slope/rate-of-spread data (upslope ~4.68x downslope at 30 degrees). Not an evacuation work; it is a candidate input for a NOVELTY_STANDARD §4(a) argument that Korean slope distributions compress evacuation lead times.

title: Forest Fire Risk Prediction in South Korea Using Google Earth Engine: Comparison of Machine Learning Models
authors: Choi, Jukyeong; Yun, Young-Jo; Chae, Heemun
one_line_difference: Nationwide Korean ignition-risk mapping from twelve Earth-Engine covariates; occurrence risk only, no spread, no evacuation, no timing.

title: Developing a New Hourly Forest Fire Risk Index Based on Catboost in South Korea
authors: Kang, Yoojin; Jang, Eunna; Im, Jungho; Kwon, Chungeun; Kim, Sungyong
one_line_difference: Hourly 1 km ignition-risk index for Korea benchmarked against the operational DWI and a modified FFMC; an occurrence-risk product, with no spread, no evacuation and no timing.

title: Major wildfires in Korea [translation]
authors: Korea Forest Service (산림청)
venue: Korea Forest Service official website, 산림재난 > 산불 > 산불정보 (cmsId=FC_001157)
one_line_difference: Source of record for Korean major-fire burned area and duration. Not a research work; cite only for event statistics, never as evidence about evacuation methods.

title: Forest Fire Statistics Yearbook (2025) [translation]
authors: Korea Forest Service (산림청)
venue: Korea Forest Service, Daejeon (대전); annual statistical series
one_line_difference: Official annual wildfire statistics; the data source behind e-나라지표 indicator 1309. Not peer-reviewed and not a modelling work.

title: The Analysis of Forest Fire Fuel Structure Through the Development of Crown Fuel Vertical Distribution Model: A Case Study on Managed and Unmanaged Stands of Pinus densiflora in the Gyeongbuk Province
authors: Lee, Sun Joo (이선주); Kwon, Chun Geun (권춘근); Kim, Sungyong (김성용)
venue: Korean Journal of Agricultural and Forest Meteorology / 한국농림기상학회지
one_line_difference: Measured Pinus densiflora crown fuel vertical distribution and canopy bulk density (~1.6x higher in unmanaged stands) in Gyeongbuk — Korean fuel-structure evidence usable as a crown-fire input, with no evacuation content of its own.

title: Spatial Prediction of Forest Fire Occurrence Integrating Human Proximity: A Machine Learning Approach for Korea's Eastern Coast
authors: Lee, Jeman; Ahn, Sujung; Im, Sangjun
one_line_difference: Random-forest ignition-probability layer (30 m) intended to sit alongside the operational KFDRI for patrol prioritisation on Korea's east coast; it predicts WHERE a fire starts, never when anyone should move.

title: Predicting Forest Fire Danger Using Fuel Characteristics of Forest
authors: Lim, Chan Jin; Chae, Heemun
venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Hazard Mitigation / 한국방재학회논문집
one_line_difference: Field-measured surface and crown fuel loads at 12 Gangwon sites converted to fire intensity (kW/m) and a four-class danger rating via Van Wagner's crown-fire criterion — Korean fuel evidence, no evacuation decision.

title: Application of the Canadian Fire Weather Index for Forest Fire Danger Assessment in South Korea
authors: Lim, Chan Jin; Chae, Hee Mun
one_line_difference: Transfers the Canadian FWI to Korea over 2004-2023 and reports it tracks Korean large-fire frequency when regionally calibrated; a danger-climatology result with no decision output.

title: The Value of Climatological, Categorical and Probabilistic Forecasts in the Cost-Loss Ratio Situation
authors: Murphy; Allan H.
one_line_difference: Murphy owns the cost-loss decision-analytic framework and the relative-value measure for a generic two-action/two-event protective decision; he does not model a spatial hazard, an evacuation mission, or a positional trigger comparator.

title: Assessing the economic value of weather forecasts: an overview of methods, results and issues
authors: Murphy; Allan H.
one_line_difference: A survey of forecast-value methodology; establishes that the whole apparatus WildfireGuardian would use for RQ1 was already mature in 1994.

title: Singular Vectors, Metrics, and Adaptive Observations
authors: Palmer, T. N.; Gelaro, R.; Barkmeijer, J.; Buizza, R.
one_line_difference: Founds targeted/adaptive observation: where to observe is chosen by sensitivity of a forecast metric, and the correct metric depends on the PURPOSE of the observations; the purpose is forecast-error reduction, not a downstream protective-action decision, and the domain is synoptic meteorology.

title: Climatic and Forest Drivers of Wildfires in South Korea (1980-2024): Trends, Predictions, and the Role of the Wildland-Urban Interface
authors: Park, Jin-chan; Suh, Ji-Hoon; Baek, Minho
one_line_difference: Regression/ML attribution over 905 Korean fires: each +1 m/s peak wind expands burned area by ~8.5 ha and each +1% RH reduces it by ~3 ha, with conifer dominance amplifying spread. Korean-specific evidence for why peak gusts, not mean wind, govern Korean lead times — an input to a §4(a) argument, not an evacuation study.

title: Modern Bayesian Experimental Design
authors: Rainforth, Tom; Foster, Adam; Ivanova, Desi R.; Bickford Smith, Freddie
pages: 100-114 (page range from secondary source; Crossref page field empty)
one_line_difference: Canonical modern review of Bayesian experimental design / expected information gain; confirms the machinery WG-C-008 would use is mature and not ours to claim as a method.

title: Skill and relative economic value of the ECMWF ensemble prediction system
authors: Richardson; D. S.
venue: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society
one_line_difference: Owns the relative-economic-value (REV) curve as a function of cost-loss ratio and lead time for ensemble forecasts; the 'region of the C/L axis where the forecast has value' IS a forecast-value boundary, but in weather- variable space, with climatology as the reference, not a tuned spatial trigger buffer.

title: From Reactive to Active Sensing: A Survey on Information Gathering in Decision-theoretic Planning
authors: Veiga, Tiago; Renoux, Jennifer
one_line_difference: Survey establishing active information gathering in decision-theoretic planning as a mature field with its own taxonomy; nothing wildfire-specific and no deadline-constrained protective-action instantiation.
